title: Ironsail Maritime knowledgebot onramp notes
content:
Context:
- 2025-11-12 intro call with Ironsail Maritime (ops + IT + procurement). They run a fleet of small cargo vessels with intermittent satellite connectivity and a central dispatch in Rotterdam. Primary ask: lightweight knowledgebot to assist deck officers with operational checklists, port procedures, customs docs, and first-pass troubleshooting for engine alerts (not diagnostics).

High-level constraints / customer requirements (raw):
- Must work reliably with intermittent WAN. Shipboard LAN + onboard appliance preferred; central cloud as fallback.
- Data residency: some manifests/crew data cannot leave customer network (jurisdictional). Need Private (on-prem/VPC) deployment option.
- Latency: interactive Q&A within 1.5s local P50 for the on-device assistant; remote queries OK up to 3s.
- Model footprint: target inference on a single A100-equivalent or smaller (they prefer lower-power GPUs like T4/p4d). Consider quantized 4-bit variant.
- Token budget & cost: they expect high volume on routine queries (checklists) — need aggressive caching/prefix reuse.
- Safety/compliance: redact PII from logs; audit trail for each query.
- Offline fallback: local LLM fallback when disconnected; queue and sync events when reconnected.
- Integration: Slack-like onboard comms app + terminal interface. Also must be callable from their FleetOps API (internal).

Notes from call (bullet brain-dump):
- Ops lead (Captain Henrik) cares about checklist accuracy and traceability — wants every bot suggestion stamped with "source: policy x.y" when pulling from procedures.
- IT (Lea) emphasized locked-down network: no egress from appliance except to the control-plane for heartbeats; approves outbound only via proxy + mTLS.
- Procurement: procurement wants two pricing options: hosted pilot (3 months) vs private appliance + 12-month support.
- Concern: OS-level updates on ships are slow; ISO images must be easy to apply and rollback.
- They already use an on-prem knowledge repo (Confluence + S3-like object store) and a telemetry store (InfluxDB). Need connectors.
- Typical queries: "Port arrival checklist - Oslo"; "How to isolate fuel pump fault code F12"; "Customs doc template for Iceland import" (templates must be surfaced).
- Security: HSM/KMS for key material on the appliance; RBAC maps to crew roles (captain, chief engineer, shore-support).

Technical gotchas / risks we flagged:
- Intermittent connectivity means KV cache strategies must be durable across restarts and power cycles (persist to local NVMe).
- Model variant fallbacks: ensure canned-policy responses when model not available (e.g., bring up last-synced doc snippet).
- Telemetry bandwidth constraints: ship can't stream token-level logs constantly; need sampling/summary.
- Model hallucination risk on engineering troubleshooting — embed references + highlight confidence bands.
- Edge appliance sizing: unclear if T4 is sufficient for targeted latency at peak concurrency (deck + engine room simultaneous queries). We should run a sizing test with realistic prompts.

Suggested technical approach (initial proposal sketch):
1) Provision a private appliance image (container + control plane agent) for shipboard deployment. Appliance has: lightweight model server (supports quantized llama-like model), local KV cache persisted on NVMe, local Confluence connector to sync policy docs (one-way pull), secure sync queue for telemetry/usage to shore when connected.
2) Model selection: start with a 7B quantized variant optimized for CPU/GPU hybrid (we recommend quantized 8-bit or 4-bit PTQ depending on runtime). Reserve a fallback deterministic template engine for checklist responses when confidence < threshold.
3) Caching: prefix-level cache for common checklist prompts + per-ship static snips. Use TTL + manual sync commands for immediate policy updates.
4) Auth & keys: integrate with customer KMS; allow import of public key + trust anchor. mTLS enforced to control plane.
5) Observability: local UI for per-query logs (redacted), sampled telemetry shipped when bandwith permits. Admin console to view sync queue and conflict resolution for doc updates.
6) Testing plan: stage 0 synthetic prompts (our infra), stage 1 on-appliance load test at port, stage 2 limited onboard pilot on 2 vessels for 6 weeks.

Action items & owners (from meeting):
- Maya: draft first-pass SOW + pilot pricing options (due 2025-11-20).
- Diego: prototype appliance image with local KV persistence + Confluence connector; run quick perf on T4 vs A100 baseline (due 2025-12-05).
- Priya: security checklist for KMS/HSM + network hardening guide (due 2025-11-30).
- Samir: schedule sizing run with infra team and estimate costs (due 2025-11-25).
- Customer (Lea/Henrik): provide sample Confluence space export + telemetry throughput numbers (action: share by 2025-11-18).

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Can Ironsail accept a container-based appliance (OCI image) or do they need a bare-metal ISO? (Lea to confirm).
- Which GPU types are allowed on their ship appliance (power budget)? Need spec sheet.
- Exact PII redaction policy and retention window — compliance will need to sign off.
- How will model updates be authorized and rolled out across fleet safely? need canary policy.

Meeting artifacts to assemble for customer follow-up (my plan):
- One-pager outlining hosted vs private pricing with latency/guarantee tradeoffs (include cost per concurrent deck-user).
- Pilot plan doc with success criteria (latency, checklist accuracy, sync reliability).
- Appliance runbook: install steps, rollback, emergency offline mode.
- Data flow diagram (local-only vs synced).

Quick notes to self / heuristics for engineering sync:
- Prioritize fast NVMe-backed KV with atomic commits — avoid cache corruption on power loss.
- Add a deterministic fallback templating layer for checklist answers to eliminate hallucinations for critical ops instructions.
- Make telemetry sampling configurable by ship (bandwidth varies wildly).
- Add a "source attribution" header for any doc-sourced snippet returned to crew (very important to Captain).

Next meeting: pilot scoping call w/ procurement + IT + ops. I suggested week of 2025-11-24. Diego to present preliminary perf numbers; Priya to cover security posture.

Misc scribbles:
- Potential competitor risk: ShipAI out of Norway has a prebuilt marine checklist product. Emphasize auditability & integration depth as our differentiator.
- Procurement asked about SLA credits for offline periods — flag for commercial.

End of note.
